para.text: Defines the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund;
Sets forth the responsibilities of the Maryland Department of Health with respect to the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund;
Describes the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission;
Identifies eligible applicants for the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund; and
Outlines the grant process for the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Administrative expenses” means staffing costs, costs associated with establishing and maintaining the Commission, and costs associated with the development, review, evaluation, and award of grants.
Applicant.
“Applicant” means an organization who applies to receive a grant under the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
“Applicant” includes an authorized representative acting on behalf of, or submitting an application on behalf of, an organization.

“Applied research” means research that is focused on determining how the research enterprise can most effectively translate existing scientific information into solutions to real-world problems, including new diagnostics and therapies for diseases.
“Basic research” means experimental or theoretical work undertaken to acquire new knowledge or understanding of cancer.
“Capital expenditures” means money spent to add or expand property, equipment, and assets that will benefit a grantee in the long term.
“Clinical research” means research:
Conducted primarily on patients; and
Designed to answer questions about the etiology, prevention, early detection, diagnosis, or treatment of cancer.
“Commission” means the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission as established in Health-General Article, §20-121, Annotated Code of Maryland.

“Community-based participatory research” means a collaborative, partnership approach to research that equitably involves community members, organizational representatives, and researchers in all aspects of the research process.
“Department” means the Maryland Department of Health.
Educational Institution.
“Educational institution” means an organization whose primary mission is to educate individuals.
“Educational institution” includes:
Colleges;
Universities; and
Graduate schools.
“Fund” means the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
Grant.
“Grant” means financial assistance from the State to support an applicant's activities related to pediatric cancer research.
“Grant” does not mean a contract.
“Grantee” means an organization who receives a grant under the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.
“Hospital” means an institution that is licensed in the State under COMAR 10.07.01 or other applicable standards established by the jurisdiction or state in which the service is provided.

“Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund” means the program which is administered by the Department under Health-General Article, §20-120, Annotated Code of Maryland, to provide grants to nonprofit hospitals, educational institutions, and other nonprofit organizations to conduct pediatric cancer research.
“Nonprofit organization” means an organization that is classified under §501(c)(3) of the Internal Revenue Code as a nonprofit organization.
Research.
“Research” means activities to develop or advance the understanding of cancer or the techniques or modalities effective in the prevention, cure, screening, diagnosis, or treatment of cancer.
“Research” includes applied, basic, clinical, translational, and community-based participatory research.
“Secretary” means the Secretary of the Maryland Department of Health.
“State-based childhood cancer organization” means a social organization as defined by State Finance and Procurement Article, §7-402(a), Annotated Code of Maryland that:
Is headquartered in the State; and
Has a primary mission to address childhood cancer.
“Translational research” means using or applying new discoveries to benefit patient care.
The Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund is a non-lapsing, special fund created by Health-General Article, §20-120, Annotated Code of Maryland, for pediatric cancer research, which is generated from:
Money appropriated in the State Budget to the Fund; and
Any other donations to the Fund.
Department Expenditure of Fund. The Department may only expend funds:
In accordance with an appropriation approved by the General Assembly in the annual State budget; or
Through an approved budget amendment under State Finance and Procurement Article, §§7-209 and 7-210, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Approved Utilization of the Fund. The Fund shall be used only:
To make grants for pediatric cancer research;
For administrative expenses; and

To distribute to a promotional account to be allocated to a State-based childhood cancer organization to be used to promote further donations to the Fund and to educate the State scientific community about opportunities for childhood cancer research through the Fund.
Each fiscal year, the Secretary may distribute and use no more than a total of 5 percent of the Fund for the purposes referenced in §C(2) and (3) of this regulation.
Any unspent portions of the Fund shall remain in the Fund and may not revert to the General Fund of the State.
Money expended from the Fund is supplemental to, and is not intended to take the place of, funding that would otherwise be appropriated to the Department for pediatric cancer research.
Administer the Fund;
Submit a report annually to the General Assembly on administration of the Fund;
Each fiscal year, decide on the amount from the Fund to be distributed to:
The promotional account;
Administrative expenses; and
Pediatric cancer research grants; and
Use the Fund to implement activities related to:
The promotional account;
Administrative expenses; and
Pediatric cancer research grants.

section.heading: Responsibilities of the Pediatric Cancer Research Commission.

para.text: The Commission oversees the award of competitive grants from the Fund.
Duties of the Commission. The Commission shall:
Develop the criteria, standards, and requirements for the review of applications for pediatric cancer research grants from the Fund;
Establish procedures and guidelines to be used in the review, evaluation, ranking, and rating of the research grant proposals;
Develop criteria and a process for reviewing grant applications to ensure that each application is complete and satisfies the criteria, standards, and requirements developed by the Commission;
Develop disclosure and recusal guidelines to be followed by members of the Commission when considering grant applications;
Ensure participation recusal is conducted in accordance with the guidelines required by §B(4) of this regulation;
Establish standards for the oversight of awards; and
Conduct progress reviews of grant recipients.
The Commission may consult with experts in performing its duties.

section.heading: Eligible Applicants for Pediatric Cancer Research Grants.

para.text: Subject to any limitations imposed under §B of this regulation, applicants eligible to receive grants from the Department under Regulation .04D(3) of this chapter include:
Nonprofit hospitals;
Educational institutions; and
Other nonprofit organizations the Department determines to be eligible.
The Department may limit the applicants eligible to receive a grant in §A of this regulation based on:
Availability of funds;
The Department's ability to account for and monitor the grant funding;
The qualifications of the applicants; or
The ability of the applicants to comply with requirements of the grant.

section.heading: Allowable Uses of the Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Funds.
section.text: Funds granted for pediatric cancer research under Regulation .04D(3) of this chapter may be used for:

para.text: Applied research;
Basic research;
Clinical research;
Community-based participatory research; or
Translational research.

section.heading: Unallowable Uses of Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Funds.
section.text: A grantee may not use grant funds from the Fund to pay for:

para.text: Renovations;
Capital expenditures;
Institutional overhead expenses, organizational expenses, or charges that are not directly related to pediatric cancer research;
Expenses arising from community-based support services; or
Individual-level prevention, cure, screening, diagnosis, or treatment that is unrelated to a research project eligible for the Fund.

section.heading: Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Funding and Application.

para.text: Each fiscal year, the Department:
Shall determine the amount of funding available for pediatric cancer research grants; and
May consider awarding funding for grant applications for pediatric cancer research.
The Department shall make available the grant application and its instructions.
An applicant may not apply for grant funding for more than 2 years with a single grant application.
An applicant shall submit the completed application packet to the Department by the due date provided by the Department to be eligible for award consideration.
Each Maryland educational institution shall be considered as a singular entity, including:
The University System of Maryland and University of Maryland Medical System, including all their campuses and health entities;

The Johns Hopkins University and Johns Hopkins Medical Institutions, including all their campuses and health entities, the Kennedy Krieger Institute, and the Lieber Institute for Brain Development; and
All subsidiaries and locations of any other organization.
As part of the application for a pediatric cancer research grant under §D of this regulation, an applicant shall attest that the applicant:
Will use grant funds solely in accordance with the grant requirements;
Will conduct the pediatric cancer research for which the grant is requested in the State;
Has the legal capacity and all necessary legal authority to incur the obligations related to the grant award; and
Will comply with all applicable State and federal laws.

section.heading: Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Application Review and Approval.

para.text: The Commission, to review the grant applications that are submitted for funding under the Fund, may:
Develop one or more review committees; or
Contract with one or more external peer review consultants.
If a review committee or external peer review consultant is used for the purposes described in §A of this regulation:
The review committee or external peer review consultant shall make a recommendation to the Commission about the merits, rank, and rating of each application; and
The Commission shall then evaluate the review committee or external consultant’s report of each application.
The Commission shall recommend to the Department which projects should be funded.
The Department shall make the final determination on funding grant applications.
Grantees shall be subject to progress reviews on a schedule set by the Department.
The Commission, to conduct progress reviews and make recommendations to the Department about each grantee’s progress, may:
Develop one or more review committees; or
Contract with one or more external peer review consultants.
The Commission shall recommend to the Department whether to continue providing grant funds to each grantee.
The Department shall make the final determination on whether to continue providing grant funds to each grantee.

A grantee may apply to the Department for a no-cost extension of the grant period for the award before the expiration of the grant period by submitting a written request for an extension to the Department.
In evaluating whether to recommend an extension of the grant period, the Commission:
Shall assess whether progress has been made on the grant project; and
May recommend to the Department that an extension be granted based on reports submitted under Regulation .13 of this chapter.
The Department shall consider the Commission’s recommendation regarding the request for an extension and may approve a no-cost grant extension for up to 1 year.

section.heading: Payments, Terms and Conditions of Pediatric Cancer Research Grant Awards, and Terminations.

para.text: If a financial or progress report required in §B or C of this regulation is overdue, the Department may withhold payment to the grantee until the report is submitted.
Financial Reports and Records.
A grantee shall:
Establish a separate account to track expenditures under the grant;
Maintain accurate records, including documentation of each transaction pertaining to the grant;
Submit to the Department invoices for payment by the deadline specified by the Department;

Submit to the Department a final financial expenditure report containing the signature of the financial officer or designee of the entity affiliated with the grant award by the deadline specified by the Department; and
Submit a refund of any unexpended funds by the deadline specified by the Department.

The Department may audit the accounts referenced in §B(1) of this regulation at any time up to 3 years from the date the final financial expenditure report is submitted under §B(1) of this regulation.
A grantee shall retain all records pertaining to a grant award for 3 years from the date the final financial expenditure report is submitted under §B(1) of this regulation.
In the case of an audit or litigation, the Department may extend the time period under §B(2) or (3) of this regulation until the completion of the audit or litigation.
Progress Reports.
A grantee shall submit to the Department:
An interim report describing the progress of the grant by the deadline specified by the Department; and
A comprehensive final report by the deadline specified by the Department.
The Commission shall conduct oversight and progress reviews of grant recipients using reports submitted to the Department, site visits, or any other mechanism to be determined by the Commission.
The Department shall keep research results confidential as required by Health-General Article, §§4-101—4-103, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Publication of Research.
A grantee who publishes results from activities shall include in the publication an acknowledgement with the text: “Supported in part with funds from the Maryland Pediatric Cancer Fund.”
A grantee shall provide the Department with a copy of any published article pertaining to the activities conducted under the grant.
Ownership of Equipment. A grantee:
Shall ensure that equipment purchased under a grant under this chapter is used for the sole purpose of the grant;
Shall keep an inventory of all equipment purchased; and
May not transfer the equipment to another entity without the written permission of the Department.
Termination.
The Secretary may terminate a grant:
If a grantee fails to comply with:
The requirements of this chapter; or
State, federal, and municipal laws applicable to the performance of research under the grant;
If a grantee fails to carry out the purposes for which the grant was awarded;
In compliance with a court order; or
At the request of the grantee.
The Department and the State may not be responsible for any expenses incurred by a grantee after cancellation of a grant.
The grantee shall return all unexpended funds to the Department within 60 calendar days of termination of a grant.
Compliance with Existing Laws. A grantee shall ensure that an activity conducted in the performance of the grant is in compliance with all State, federal, and local laws.
Liability.
A grantee is solely responsible for their actions pertaining to research conducted under a grant award; and
The State and the Department may not be liable for any claims, losses, liabilities, expenses, or damages arising from research conducted under a grant awarded under this chapter.
A grantee shall enter into a grant agreement with the Department.
